item.title: SCP: Kingdom Come my first tale
item.description: The book of revelations with SCPs, inspired by DC's Kingdom Come
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

page type tale

genre: horror

page layout a transcript of a conversation with passages from the book revelations used as a framing device

Elevator pitch: Going off of what was established in the tale "new job". A former researcher on his death bed shares visions of an apocalyptic battle between SCP-999 and the scarlet king.

central narrative: while being read his last rites, the dying man interrupts the priest and starts yelling about his visions. The priest tries to tell him to save his strength, but the man insists he must listen. The visions begin with a great war between the SCP foundation and 6 other groups of interests, the war being about weather to destroy anomalies, study them, or let them be. The War comes to a head with an all out seige on site 19, where SCP-988 is being kept. During the battle, SCP-999 supposedly dies to save a researcher from SCP-049. That researcher then finds and opens SCP-988 The visions then skip ahead to the end of the seige, where SCP-053 and 682 are united and release some of the most dangerous SCPs. The survivors of the ensuing chaos come together despite their differences to try and stop this army of SCPs, and the Scarlet king feeds off the chaos of this battle. Pretty soon a portal to the scarlet king's world rips open and fire rains down as the Scarlet king enters our world. Just then SCP-999 reappears with a handful of other thaumiel class SCPs. Unfortunately the man dies before he can tell the man how it ends, but he does leave him with a warning not to "face the light when the day comes" before passing away.

hook: its an end of the world prediction that sorta lines up with the book of revelations.

item.title: A (Real) Cognitohazard
item.content:encoded:
Hi,

I'm planning on writing a meta SCP article on the McCollough effect. Thing is, I suppose you could say this is a real-life cognitohazard. Viewing the images can alter the way your brain perceives colour, causing long-lasting changes to colour perception. In some cases, the effects have lasted months after initial viewing.

I could totally do this… there are McCollough images that are CC compliant. Thing is, this could affect people in real life. I guess I would need some sort of disclaimer warning the reader of the image, but people are just going to assume the warning is fictional. It's not, and these images can alter you in real life.

I don't know how to write a disclaimer that will properly inform the reader of the potential repercussions whilst not breaking the tone of the site.

item.title: The Blur *Seeking Greenlights*
item.description: an SCP article about a mysterious shadow
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is as the name suggest, a blur or as also seen as a shadow. It inhabits the very south of Argentina, the being is observed to have human level or higher intelligence and exhibits some anomalous abilities.

Central Narrative: This SCP is on close watch by the foundation, it having no physical body and only appearing as a semi transparent blur or a shadow makes it impossible to contain. So the foundation has decided to watch it via satellite. While it is not hostile towards anything, it has been observed to kill plant based life around it, likely by an unconscious ability to soak moisture from its surroundings. The foundation has no clear hypothesis for its existence but the most widely accepted one is that the SCP is an alternate dimensional being that exist on a semi 4 dimensional level, allowing it to have no physical body, yet still visible to 3 dimensional beings, although this theory is not proven.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP here has a lot of mystery around it, and I want to be able to not have a definitive answer what it exactly is. While the article will be mostly field notes by observers, I also want to explain why this SCP is as smart as a human and what ties it has to earth.

Additional Notes: I cant really explain everything here but if I can obtain 2 greenlights and make a sandbox, I can go into much better detail about this SCP and why it exist. Im not entirely sure where I can improve the central narrative to make it sound more interesting, but I have many ideas for this SCP so shoot your criticism at me so I can make this sound even more like a true SCP

item.title: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight)
item.description: an interdimensional, aquatic SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, and a narrative inter spliced with exploration logs and journal entries

Elevator Pitch: Life came from the cold, dark crushing depths of the sea, and that is where it is most safe, supposedly

Central Narrative: Talassaphobia is the fear of deep ocean, and is super common, but at the same time the ocean is considered to be the origin of all life. This SCP concept takes it to a new level: that beneath the deepest oceanic point on earth, the world is connected to a vast, interdimensional ocean. This ocean/SCP connects to different, life bearing universes, and in itself holds no deadly anomalies. Living things entering this ocean go into a catatonic state and cannot be hurt or killed. The article can explore strange, normal animals that have entered and been affected by the space's effects, as well as exploration of the space. The main narrative doesn't exactly focus on it being this big inter dimensional space though, and is more about the small team of researchers that are for the most part left alone researching it. Along the ideas of “if you stare long enough into the abyss…” theming. While the main SCP may seem big, it is really more about how the people left alone with what would be consider a “safe” sort of anomaly do their best not to lose themselves in it, and what happens to the things that fail.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP takes a common fear and twists it into something welcoming. If you're familiar with the abyss from Dark Souls its similar: more of the pitch black being the true, calm nature of life and less so the rampaging monsters. It expires isolation, survival, and twisting the notion of what the deep ocean is like.

item.title: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.description: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image
item.content:encoded:
At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in some apartment in Iran.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Elevator Pitch: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in an abandoned apartment in Iran.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation is compelled to visit an apartment that everybody, including other agencies concerned with the anomalous, seemed to know about. It turns out that the anomaly is not the apartment itself, but a bonsai tree sitting in the bedroom. The Foundation takes over the entire apartment complex, "managing" it to keep appearances. The apartment, officially the containment cell for the anomaly, looked to be lived in, but beyond writings and personal belongings of the tenant, there are no records of residence.

+ show block
– hide block

They find out that the bonsai tree emits radio signals through an invisible root system throughout the Earth. These radio signals cause those exposed to them for prolonged periods to feel intense dread and regret. Not much else learned about the bonsai tree, and the former tenant is still at large.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Knowledge of an object suddenly enters the collective unconscious.

Additional Notes: What I really want to highlight is the juxtaposition between the ubiquity of the bonsai tree within the collective unconscious and the anonymity of the original tenant. In summary, the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread, while the tenant, seemingly untrackable, is like an unobtainable goal.

While drafting this idea, I kept having trouble with suggesting the meaning of the tree's radio signals and the significance of the date in which it manifested. The idea is that the tree sort of feeds off of people's anxieties, and the "root system" connects to the minds of every person on Earth. The problem is that I don't want to be overt about it.

I'm not looking to write something scary or unsettling. I just want to make something that's curious.

item.title: A Canary In The Coal Mine
item.description: The story of researchers researching other researchers.
item.content:encoded:
The story of researchers researching other researchers. When the lines between 'tester' and 'testee' become blurred.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama

Page Layout (Optional): It will begin with a standard SCP article structure, followed by a series of experiment logs, journal extracts and Foundation documents explaining the story of the discovery of the subject.

Elevator Pitch: One day a researcher discovers a strange correlation between co-worker drinking a specific brand of soda and disasters/containment breaches occuring to their projects which he is certain is a viable "warning-light" to help contain dangerous SCPs.

Central Narrative: An anonomous researcher in one of the foundation sites has been secretly classified as a thaumiel class SCP, used as an early warning system for potential disasters that may befall foundation projects. Should this researcher drink a can of soda of a brand they typically claim to hate, it is a sign that a project which the researcher is assigned to will have a some form of disaster occur to it.

+ show block
– hide block

One observant co-worker, Dr. Gables, notices this trend and begins documenting it. What follows is a series of test logs and journal extracts of Dr. Gables investigating this anomouly and putting the paperwork in to give the researcher an official SCP designation. As the logs go on, experiments ramp up and start getting strange. By the time Dr. Gables has orchestrated an entire breach event resulting in multiple deaths, we realise that he had been operating without foundation clearance the entire time.

He uses an edited version of his obervations (with his involvment having been removed) to get the researcher an official SCP designation. Following a few more experiments, Dr. Gables goes insane and assaults the researcher. Following this, the Foundation investigates Dr. Gables to find his original observations that proved his involvement in multiple incidents, as well as numorous logs documenting other Foundation personnel and a large amount of blackmail which he has been using to get away with his actions. This concludes with a notice of termination of Dr. Gables and the reassignment of the SCP project to another researcher.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dynamics of the relationships between Foundation researchers as well as the covert workings of a researcher with their own agendas and goals.

Additional Notes: I'm scared that readers may lose interest before getting to the meat of the story which would take place in the experiment logs and other attached documents.

Central Narrative: Corpse was found frozen in Yukon when villagers noticed a strange, unidentified creature moving erratically. Corpse's lower half is controlled by a series of live neurons that consume the bone and ligament tissue and shock the muscles into moving convulsively, allowing it to crawl. It will violently hyperextend its joints (bending knees backwards and such) and break its own bones to move.

+ show block
– hide block

The live neuron DNA matches the dead woman, whose brain is somewhat shrunken, or possibly her fetus. Lead scientist believes it's capable of navigation and is searching for something, but regrets that its lifespan is so short as a result of consuming its own flesh and progressively deflating in size, that they'll never know what it wants. It must remain frozen to stay alive until the foundation finds a way to save it or find what it's looking for.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Using body horror as a focus, of which I haven't seen much here, and a full story with open-ended conclusion that is coherent with beginning, middle, and end if the reader reads between the lines. Specifically, I'd like to include a voiceover file from the scientist's observation session with written transcript, recording the skittering and cracking noises the skip makes, with a subtle hint/easter egg for readers to listen for, revealing what it's capable of, and possibly answering the question of what it actually wants (this won't be included in the transcript, so that the reader is left to think and interpret it on their own).

- Elevator Pitch

This scp is, in a sense, humanity's seeming desire to leave earth's atmosphere and explore outer space. This scp was discovered once the foundation began to notice strange patterns in the direction and movement of every human and manmade object launched into space, as well as every other object in space (planets, stars, etc), which all appear to be converging to an unknown spot in spacetime at irregular speeds.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

While investigating several other space related anomalies, the foundation begins to put together a strange pattern in the movement of every object that has been launched into space, which all eventually begin to travel in the same exact direction. Digging further, they find a cut section of the Apollo 11 landing, during which mike collins seems to jump and be dragged out in this exact same direction for a few seconds, contrary to the observed gravitational effects of the moon. Curiously, satelites in orbit around earth such as the ISS are unaffected, as well as celestial bodies such as the planets, moons, and sun. However, calculations run by the foundation indicate that these bodies only appear to be unaffected, and have actually been moving in an even pace to one another in this direction for a while. Finally, the foundation uncovers that, over the course of millenia, every object in the universe has been traveling towards a single undefined point in space.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ Hook/Attention Grabber
- Hook/Attention Grabber

After running some tests, the foundation manages to calculate the coordinates for this point. After a predictably long journey, they finally manage to send a ship to the coordinates, which finds a barely describable fold in spacetime where all things are seemingly erased. Ordered to return, the unmanned ship curiously defies its controls and moves towards the fold, and strong radio interference is heard as the ship displays a white void. The foundation finds the sounds to be their only lead, and work to decipher a potential meaning. Although they fail, an incident occurs where these sounds are heard again from the sky, this time being mysteriously comprehensible, with the message:
"You have protected your world
from a great many threats,
from those which are incomprehensible,
and for that I am proud.
But what comes now you are not prepared for,
nor am I,
so I must protect you now,
within my unwavering.
Join me,
In this void,
and travel ever upward,
for you have no other choice"

The article ends with a question: If after all the foundation has fought, this void only interferes now, then what exactly is coming for us?

item.title: Individual Rating Modules for Log Entries
item.description: Perhaps an easier way to quality-control.
item.content:encoded:
Low-quality content naturally piles up in places like 682's termination log, 1459's extended logs, and other very large collaborative lists. Inevitably, a page curator has to go through and prune away the bad entries. I imagine that this is tiresome and time-consuming for the curator, and it also means that garbage entries in these logs live much longer than an equally garbage SCP would. If there were some way to install individual rating modules for each item on the log, so they could be voted on individually, then perhaps that might save some time for the curator and shorten the lifespan of the bad entries.

I thought that the log of extranormal events or unexplained locations was already like this, but it seems that I was mistaken.

item.title: 500 grains of people (seeking greenlights)
item.description: Basically 500 people from the future got turned into grains of sand
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the collective term for 500 sapient grains of sand, which all spontaneously appeared in Memphis Tennessee. They don't need to eat or drink, but they do sleep. They move around by sliding around, via anomalous means. They can all talk, but don't have any mouths, or facial features. They're all as audible as normal human beings, and are able to be killed easily, such as by stomping, throwing, etc.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The Foundation first acquires SCP-X when reports of screams in Memphis Tennessee, coming from nowhere start coming in. The Foundation investigates, and soon find the source, approximately 500 grains of sand. They take them to a site, and get the instances to pick one grain to explain what's going on.

The grain explains that they're from the year 2025, and during that year, several ginormous extraterrestrial space crafts landed on earth, and started killing every human they could find. Not animals, they left horses, dogs, everything else alone. They didn't offer surrender to the humans either.

When cities were clear of humans, the aliens started moving in to the houses, and started taking on the humans lives. Except they lacked all the problems that humans had. There weren't wars between them, they were eco friendly, using resources such as solar panels and energy supplies they had brought to earth from their ships. (The grain of sand knows this because he used to be a part of a group of humans who snuck into cities and tried to reclaim them.)

The aliens also seemed to have highly advanced technology, such as weapons that could freeze people in place, and even time machines. Eventually, almost the entire human population was wiped out. And soon the aliens began hording the last humans into chamber, where they were either vaporized, or transformed into other entities, such as animals, or plants, and even furniture. The grain of sand (who was a human at the time) was horded into a large chamber with around 500 other people. The SCP-X instance realized that the aliens operating the machine appeared to be panicking, and the machine malfunctioned, turning the 500 people into grains of sand instead of animals or furniture. It then started a countdown, and apparently went into a kind of "time travel mode", and sent them into the past.

The grains of sand all show signs of traumatization, reasonably. The file is then updated in February of 2025, stating that several ginormous extraterrestrial space crafts appeared out of a wormhole in the Earths solar system. Using information gathered from the SCP-X instances, the Foundation neutralizes the threat.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber here is the end of the world vibe the story brings about, and how there were so little survivors.

Additional Notes: This is a little idea I came up with, let me know what you think of it, I'm open to all criticism and am looking to improve!

Central Narrative: A new user joins GAW and is excited about the prospect so much he creates an anomaly get laughs and gratification from his peers. The anomaly is an amalgamation of different plant parts stitched together into the rough shape of an gun.

A vine with the back end of it curved into the spiral is the stock, a leaf clover is the trigger, the head of a Venus fly trap acts as placing ammo, a tree branch is the handguard, and a rose acts as the muzzle.

There is a specialized part that is near the Venus head, an enlarged mutated pea pod. Whenever water is poured into the mouth of the Venus head, the pod undergoes production of enlarged peas in the sack. The juices in the sack freeze the peas and they are pushed up into the chamber. Methane gases produced by manure inside the chamber ignite and propel the peas through the flower. These peas can cause damage similar to an actual bullet.

+ show block
– hide block

The newbie made this as an play on the word "Peashooter" as a joke and thought he would get a laugh from the users of GAW. Instead, they find it to be confusing, cringey, and in poor tastes. One user mentions that since it has to potential to hurt people, it counts as a lethal weapon, which goes against their rules. The Newbie profusely apologizes and promises to do better next time. The Foundation found this scp in the trash bin by an internet café.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I structured the scp this way to showcase another side of GAW, for anomalies that don't hit the mark of their liking. The whole "meat" of the article is a chat log recovered shortly after the Foundation discovers the SCP.

If any type of solid mass comes in contact with the SCP, it will sense the matter and disintegrate it completely until it doesn't sense any more solid mass. If there's no contact with solid matter it will “deactivate” and enter into a fetal position, darkening its color.

This SCP is blind but sound waves will attract the creature. It has an audible range of 30kHz, higher than any human. However it will ignore any sound or contact coming from any other non-solid element.

It has a higher density than water despite the metallic fists and its size, because of this, it stays at the surface of a liquid environment. It is suggested that his body may be made from an extremely compressed gas.

Due to this nature, if it came in contact with the geosphere, it would completely destroy the Earth's mass, ending in an XK End of the World Scenario, which is why it is classified as Keter.
